test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 29 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Two pipes, F and M, can fill a cistern in 25 minutes and 30 minutes, respectively. If both pipes are opened together, after how many minutes should pipe F be closed so that the cistern is completely filled in 15 minutes?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let Total Work = LCM(25, 30) = 150 units.

Efficiency of F = 150 ÷ 25 = 6 units/min and Efficiency of M = 150 ÷ 30 = 5 units/min.

M works for full 15 min ⇒ Work done by M = 5 × 15 = 75 units.

Remaining work = 150 − 75 = 75 units.

Time taken by F = 75 ÷ 6 = 12.5 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 12.5 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by F = 25 minutes

Time taken by M = 30 minutes

Total time = 15 minutes

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of Time Taken

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Time**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 F
 25
 150

 M
 30
 150 ÷ 30 = 5
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of F = 6 units/min

⇒ Efficiency of M = 5 units/min

⇒ Work done by M in 15 minutes = 5 × 15 = 75 units

⇒ Remaining work = 150 − 75 = 75 units

⇒ Time taken by F = Remaining Work ÷ Efficiency of F

⇒ Time taken by F = 75 ÷ 6 = 12.5 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 12.5 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM Method

Take total work as LCM of given times to simplify efficiency calculation

Efficiency Concept

Efficiency = Work ÷ Time

Partial Work Concept

If one pipe stops early, calculate remaining work separately
